root_cause.text: The cls_u32 classifier’s u32_classify() used skb_header_pointer() on computed offsets that could become negative, and that helper did not fully validate negative offsets, allowing out-of-bounds skb data access.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “skb_header_pointer() does not fully validate negative @offset values” and the fix replaces all skb_header_pointer() calls in net/sched/cls_u32.c with skb_header_pointer_careful(); the report shows this was exploitable as “KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in u32_classify”.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function body of `u32_classify()` is sufficient to determine the issue because it directly shows the packet-offset computations and dereferences used for classification. The vulnerable construct is present: the code computes dynamic offsets and then dereferences packet data without validating that the resulting offset is non-negative or within bounds. Specifically, key matching does `(*(u32*)(ptr+key->off+(off2&key->offmask))^key->val)&key->mask`, hash selection does `*(u32*)(ptr+n->sel.hoff)`, and variable offset extraction does `*(u16*)(ptr+n->sel.offoff)`. The root cause description refers to computed offsets becoming negative and causing out-of-bounds access; this code has no check preventing negative `off2`, `key->off`, `n->sel.hoff`, or `n->sel.offoff` from producing an invalid address before dereference. Also, there is no use of `skb_header_pointer()` here with safety checks; instead it directly dereferences `ptr + offset`. The only nearby check, `if (ptr < skb->tail) goto next_ht;`, is insufficient because it merely checks the base `ptr` against `skb->tail`, not the actual accessed address range, and does nothing to reject negative offsets. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present and the fix is not present.

Author: stephen hemminger <shemminger@vyatta.com>

    u32: negative offset fix
    
    It was possible to use a negative offset in a u32 match to reference
    the ethernet header or other parts of the link layer header.
    This fixes the regression caused by:
    
    commit fbc2e7d9cf49e0bf89b9e91fd60a06851a855c5d
    Author: Changli Gao <xiaosuo@gmail.com>
    Date:   Wed Jun 2 07:32:42 2010 -0700
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the exact vulnerable area inside u32_classify(). The root cause is use of skb_header_pointer() with a computed offset that may be negative. In this commit, the code changes `unsigned int toff;` to `int toff = off + key->off + (off2 & key->offmask);`, preserving signedness of the computed offset, and adds an explicit guard: `if (skb_headroom(skb) + toff < 0) goto out;` before calling `data = skb_header_pointer(skb, toff, 4, &_data);`. This is the relevant fix because it prevents accessing data when the computed offset would point before the allowed skb data area. Since the negative-offset check is present before skb_header_pointer(), the vulnerable construct is no longer present in this commit version.
